1.translation: The Lord has described the form of the Supreme Lord to be worshiped through Chapters 7–9, and has briefly shown His manifestations through statements such as “I am the taste in water,” “I am the sacrifice,” and “I am the rite.” Now, wishing to elaborate those same manifestations so that the Lord may be seen everywhere, and wishing to describe why devotion to Him must be practiced, He said: “Again, O mighty-armed one, hear My supreme word, which I shall speak to you, who take delight in the nectar of My words, out of a desire for your welfare.”
word_for_word: the form of the Supreme Lord to be worshiped
take delight in the nectar of My words
to you out of desire for your welfare

2.translation: The devas and great sages such as Bhṛgu do not know My exalted origin—My manifestation through many glories—even though I am unborn. For I am the beginning and cause of the devas and the great sages in every way, both as their producer and as the one who sets their understanding and other faculties in motion. Therefore no one knows Me without My grace.
word_for_word: the one who sets the intellect and the rest in motion

3.translation: Whoever knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great Lord of the world, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
word_for_word: the great Lord of the world
